title: Entailment-Checklist Scoring: An API-Free Alternative to LLM-Based Dense Video Caption Evaluation

contributions.purpose: Characterize why existing API-free metrics fail for checklist-based dense video caption evaluation.
contributions.mechanism: Correlate BERTScore and embedding-based similarity metrics against LLM (Gemini) judgments on checklist keypoint coverage and inspect induced system rankings.
contributions.evaluation: BERTScore shows negative correlation (-0.052 Spearman) with LLM judgments; embedding methods reach 0.409 Spearman yet invert system rankings.
contributions.source_quote: We identify that existing API-free metrics fail for checklist-based evaluation, with embedding methods inverting system rankings despite high correlation.

contributions.purpose: Provide an API-free replacement for LLM judges in checklist-based keypoint coverage scoring.
contributions.mechanism: Entailment-Checklist Scoring (ECS): a two-stage retrieve-then-verify pipeline that retrieves candidate caption sentences by embedding similarity, then verifies keypoint entailment with an open NLI model (covered(k)=1 if max P(entail|s,k) >= tau).
contributions.evaluation: On OmniDCBench, ECS is the only API-free method achieving correct system ranking (Kendall +1.0), with 71.7% keypoint accuracy and 0.511 F1 against Gemini labels.
contributions.source_quote: We propose ECS, a retrieve-then-verify pipeline that achieves correct system ranking and 71.7% keypoint accuracy with 0.511 F1 against Gemini labels.

contributions.purpose: Show that retrieval-based pruning makes API-free evaluation computationally efficient.
contributions.mechanism: Use embedding-based retrieval to prune candidate sentences before NLI verification instead of verifying all sentence-keypoint pairs.
contributions.evaluation: The retrieval stage yields a 4.8x speedup with minimal accuracy loss.
contributions.source_quote: We demonstrate 4.8x speedup through embedding-based retrieval with minimal accuracy loss, enabling efficient API-free evaluation.

self_declared_provenance.quote: Our work adapts this verifier paradigm to checklist-based caption evaluation, using NLI to determine whether specific keypoints are entailed by predicted captions.
ECS addresses this limitation by replacing LLM judges with open NLI models, enabling fully API-free evaluation while preserving the checklist structure.

notes: Method paper positioned as adapting NLI-based verification (SummaC/MENLI lineage) to SodaM-style checklist evaluation. Absolute agreement with Gemini labels is modest (0.511 F1) even though system-level ranking is perfect.
